text:
Christian Dvorak is the Flyers' tough-minutes center, and the minutes are winning right now. He has 10 points in 20 games, with five assists in his last ten, but Philadelphia has just 39.7% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. That's a hard number for any forward, and his own shot rate has dipped to 0.60 expected goals per 60 from 0.93 last season.

Context matters here. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 97th percentile competition last season, and he starts a lot of shifts in his own end. His results have also been helped a little: the Flyers have scored slightly more than their chances deserved with him out there.

He's 30, on his third team, a former London Knights scorer who became a matchup center. The line news this month put Travis Konecny back with Trevor Zegras and Dvorak, per the Northeast Times, which should help his offense. Our range has him around 48 points. If the chance share doesn't improve, the points will be harder to keep.
headline: Christian Dvorak is carrying hard minutes in Philadelphia
